request.prompt:
Job T06: usp_loss_triangle (tsql), legacy file estate/tsql/T06_usp_loss_triangle.sql (SHA-256 cee60f041de5a268d53d966f273fdde67f2a7710f57427e91412a791d568b613).
Paid loss development triangle by accident year and line of business.
Invocations, in order: run: AsOfDate=2025-12-31.

Legacy code:
/*==============================================================================
  Job      : rpt.usp_loss_triangle
  Purpose  : Paid loss development triangle for the actuarial reserving team.
             One row per accident year and line of business, with the amount
             paid in each development year (dev_0 .. dev_6) and the cumulative
             paid to date (cumulative_0 .. cumulative_6) as at @AsOfDate. Feeds
             the chain-ladder workbook for the quarterly reserving review.
  Author   : CNM

  Change log
    2019-04-08  CNM   Initial version (CR-0862)
    2019-10-21  CNM   Travel added to the triangle (CR-0947)
    2020-09-14  PD    Payments keyed with a date before the loss left out
                      (INC-2318)
    2021-02-01  PD    Unkeyed payments (NULL amount) left out
    2022-01-17  EOS   Seven accident years. Cells after the as-at date now NULL
                      instead of 0, as the workbook expects (CR-1405)
    2023-06-26  EOS   lob_code trimmed and upper-cased before grouping
                      (INC-2851)
==============================================================================*/
SET NOCOUNT ON;
GO
IF OBJECT_ID(N'rpt.loss_triangle_paid', N'U') IS NULL
CREATE TABLE rpt.loss_triangle_paid (
    accident_year  INT            NOT NULL,
    lob_code       VARCHAR(5)     NOT NULL,
    dev_0          DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    dev_1          DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    dev_2          DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    dev_3          DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    dev_4          DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    dev_5          DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    dev_6          DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    cumulative_0   DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    cumulative_1   DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    cumulative_2   DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    cumulative_3   DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    cumulative_4   DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    cumulative_5   DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    cumulative_6   DECIMAL(14,2)  NULL,
    as_of_date     DATE           NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_loss_triangle_paid PRIMARY KEY (accident_year, lob_code)
);
GO
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE rpt.usp_loss_triangle
    @AsOfDate DATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    DECLARE @job_name VARCHAR(128) = 'rpt.usp_loss_triangle',
            @as_at_yr INT          = YEAR(@AsOfDate),
            @rows     INT;

    BEGIN TRY
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'Start',
             @status = 'STARTED';

        ------------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 1. Claims with a loss in the last seven accident years
        ------------------------------------------------------------------
        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#claims') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #claims;

        SELECT c.claim_id,
               c.loss_date,
               YEAR(c.loss_date)        AS accident_year,
               UPPER(RTRIM(c.lob_code)) AS lob_code
        INTO   #claims
        FROM   stg.claims AS c WITH (NOLOCK)
        WHERE  YEAR(c.loss_date) BETWEEN @as_at_yr - 6 AND @as_at_yr
          AND  c.loss_date <= @AsOfDate;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'Load #claims',
             @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        ------------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 2. Payments to the as-at date, with their development year
        ------------------------------------------------------------------
        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#paid') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #paid;

        SELECT cl.claim_id,
               p.payment_id,
               cl.accident_year,
               cl.lob_code,
               DATEDIFF(YEAR, cl.loss_date, p.payment_date) AS dev_year,
               p.amount
        INTO   #paid
        FROM   #claims AS cl
        INNER JOIN stg.claim_payments AS p WITH (NOLOCK)
                ON p.claim_id = cl.claim_id
        WHERE  p.payment_date <= @AsOfDate
          AND  p.payment_date >  cl.loss_date   -- dated before the loss = keying error
          AND  p.amount IS NOT NULL;            -- not keyed yet

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'Load #paid',
             @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        ------------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 3. One column per development year
        ------------------------------------------------------------------
        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#tri') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #tri;

        SELECT pv.accident_year,
               pv.lob_code,
               pv.[0] AS d0, pv.[1] AS d1, pv.[2] AS d2, pv.[3] AS d3,
               pv.[4] AS d4, pv.[5] AS d5, pv.[6] AS d6
        INTO   #tri
        FROM  (SELECT accident_year, lob_code, dev_year, amount
               FROM   #paid) AS src
        PIVOT (SUM(amount) FOR dev_year IN ([0], [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6])) AS pv;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'Pivot #tri',
             @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        ------------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 4. Reload the triangle. Nothing paid yet = 0; a cell after the
        --    as-at date stays NULL.
        ------------------------------------------------------------------
        TRUNCATE TABLE rpt.loss_triangle_paid;

        INSERT INTO rpt.loss_triangle_paid
               (accident_year, lob_code, dev_0, dev_1, dev_2, dev_3, dev_4, dev_5, dev_6,
                as_of_date)
        SELECT t.accident_year,
               t.lob_code,
               ISNULL(t.d0, 0),
               CASE WHEN t.accident_year + 1 <= @as_at_yr THEN ISNULL(t.d1, 0) END,
               CASE WHEN t.accident_year + 2 <= @as_at_yr THEN ISNULL(t.d2, 0) END,
               CASE WHEN t.accident_year + 3 <= @as_at_yr THEN ISNULL(t.d3, 0) END,
               CASE WHEN t.accident_year + 4 <= @as_at_yr THEN ISNULL(t.d4, 0) END,
               CASE WHEN t.accident_year + 5 <= @as_at_yr THEN ISNULL(t.d5, 0) END,
               CASE WHEN t.accident_year + 6 <= @as_at_yr THEN ISNULL(t.d6, 0) END,
               @AsOfDate
        FROM   #tri AS t;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'Insert rpt.loss_triangle_paid',
             @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        -- cumulative paid (NULL after the as-at date, same as dev_n)
        UPDATE rpt.loss_triangle_paid
           SET cumulative_0 = dev_0,
               cumulative_1 = dev_0 + dev_1,
               cumulative_2 = dev_0 + dev_1 + dev_2,
               cumulative_3 = dev_0 + dev_1 + dev_2 + dev_3,
               cumulative_4 = dev_0 + dev_1 + dev_2 + dev_3 + dev_4,
               cumulative_5 = dev_0 + dev_1 + dev_2 + dev_3 + dev_4 + dev_5,
               cumulative_6 = dev_0 + dev_1 + dev_2 + dev_3 + dev_4 + dev_5 + dev_6;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'Cumulative paid',
             @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'End',
             @status = 'SUCCESS';
    END TRY
    BEGIN CATCH
        DECLARE @err_msg NVARCHAR(4000) = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
                @err_no  INT            = ERROR_NUMBER();

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'Error',
             @status = 'FAILED', @message = @err_msg, @error_number = @err_no;
        THROW;
    END CATCH;
END;
GO


Input tables:
- stg.claims: claim_id int (INT), claim_number string (VARCHAR(20)), policy_id int (INT), customer_id int (INT), lob_code string (VARCHAR(5)), loss_date date (DATE), reported_date date (DATE), status string (VARCHAR(12)), closed_date date (DATE), cause_code string (VARCHAR(10)), handler_code string (VARCHAR(8)), description string (NVARCHAR(200)), _row_seq int (INT)

request.system_prompt:
Translate one legacy T-SQL (SQL Server 2022) job to PySpark 4.2. Your output must reproduce the legacy output EXACTLY, record for record and value for value, bugs included: reconciliation compares every row and column with the legacy engine's own output.

Write one Python module:
- Imports only from pyspark (pyspark.sql, pyspark.sql.functions as F, pyspark.sql.types as T, pyspark.sql.Window), datetime, decimal, math, re, functools and typing.
- Exactly this entry point: def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
- inputs holds every input table by its legacy name in lower case (e.g. "stg.claims"); params holds the parameters as text (e.g. params["AsOfDate"] == "2025-12-31").
- Return a dict from each output's legacy name to a DataFrame with the output's columns. The harness then casts each column to the contract type shown, as the legacy table's insert would (so a decimal(38,6) value stored into decimal(14,2) is rounded half up).
- Never do I/O or reach engine internals: no spark.read, .write, saveAsTable, spark.conf, RDDs, UDFs, .cache(), getattr, eval, open, os or sys. spark.sql, F.expr and selectExpr only with plain string literals (no f-strings).
- Use only constants that appear in the legacy code, the parameters, or a trap card's fix guidance (format patterns, collation names). Never hard-code data values.
- Reproduce every legacy behaviour exactly, including anything that looks like a bug: never fix it. Mark each line that reproduces a suspected bug with a "# LANSH-DEFECT: <what>" comment and list the bug in defects.
- Row order: Spark has none. Wherever the result depends on order (first or last row, a running value, a cursor, NODUPKEY, RETAIN, LAG), sort on the legacy ORDER BY and then _row_seq, which every source table has in its original row order.
- Spark runs with ANSI mode on: overflow and invalid casts raise errors, and a division by zero raises; use try_divide or a guard only where the legacy engine returns NULL.

structured_output.code:
"""T06 rpt.usp_loss_triangle -> PySpark.

Paid loss development triangle by accident year and line of business, as at
params["AsOfDate"]. This reproduces the legacy T-SQL procedure exactly, legacy
defects included.
"""
import datetime
from functools import reduce

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
import pyspark.sql.functions as F
import pyspark.sql.types as T


def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
    as_of = datetime.date.fromisoformat(params["AsOfDate"].strip()[:10])
    as_at_yr = as_of.year
    as_of_lit = F.lit(as_of)

    claims = inputs["stg.claims"]
    payments = inputs["stg.claim_payments"]

    # 1. Claims with a loss in the last seven accident years
    cl = (
        claims
        .where(
            F.year("loss_date").between(as_at_yr - 6, as_at_yr)
            & (F.col("loss_date") <= as_of_lit)
        )
        .select(
            F.col("claim_id"),
            F.col("loss_date"),
            F.year("loss_date").alias("accident_year"),
            # T-SQL RTRIM strips trailing spaces only; leading spaces are kept
            F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("lob_code"))).alias("lob_code"),
        )
    )

    # 2. Payments to the as-at date, with their development year
    p = payments.select(
        F.col("claim_id").alias("p_claim_id"),
        F.col("payment_id"),
        F.col("payment_date"),
        F.col("amount"),
    )
    paid = (
        cl.join(p, p["p_claim_id"] == cl["claim_id"], "inner")
        .where(
            (F.col("payment_date") <= as_of_lit)
            & (F.col("payment_date") > F.col("loss_date"))  # LANSH-DEFECT: strict '>' drops payments made on the loss date itself, not only the ones dated before the loss
            & F.col("amount").isNotNull()
        )
        .select(
            F.col("accident_year"),
            F.col("lob_code"),
            # DATEDIFF(YEAR, a, b) counts calendar-year boundaries crossed
            (F.year("payment_date") - F.year("loss_date")).alias("dev_year"),
            F.col("amount"),
        )
    )

    # 3. PIVOT SUM(amount) FOR dev_year IN ([0]..[6]), grouped by accident_year, lob_code
    aggs = [
        F.sum(F.when(F.col("dev_year") == k, F.col("amount"))).alias("d%d" % k)
        for k in range(7)
    ]
    tri = paid.groupBy("accident_year", "lob_code").agg(*aggs)

    # 4. Insert: nothing paid yet = 0; a cell after the as-at year stays NULL
    dec = T.DecimalType(14, 2)
    zero = F.lit(0).cast(dec)

    def dev_cell(k: int):
        filled = F.coalesce(F.col("d%d" % k).cast(dec), zero)
        if k == 0:
            return filled
        return F.when(F.col("accident_year") + F.lit(k) <= F.lit(as_at_yr), filled)

    # lob_code is NOT NULL in the target: a NULL lob_code group makes the legacy INSERT fail
    lob_checked = F.when(
        F.col("lob_code").isNull(),
        F.raise_error(F.lit("Cannot insert the value NULL into column 'lob_code', table 'rpt.loss_triangle_paid'")),
    ).otherwise(F.col("lob_code"))

    ins = tri.select(
        F.col("accident_year").cast(T.IntegerType()).alias("accident_year"),
        lob_checked.alias("lob_code"),
        *[dev_cell(k).cast(dec).alias("dev_%d" % k) for k in range(7)],
    )

    # cumulative paid (NULL propagates after the as-at year, same as dev_n)
    cum_cols = []
    for k in range(7):
        expr = reduce(lambda a, b: a + b, [F.col("dev_%d" % i) for i in range(k + 1)])
        cum_cols.append(expr.alias("cumulative_%d" % k))

    out = ins.select(
        F.col("accident_year"),
        F.col("lob_code"),
        *[F.col("dev_%d" % k) for k in range(7)],
        *cum_cols,
        as_of_lit.alias("as_of_date"),
    )

    return {"rpt.loss_triangle_paid": out}

defects.intended: Leave out only payments dated before the loss (the keying error from INC-2318), which would be payment_date >= loss_date. Payments on the loss date belong in dev_0.
defects.title: Payments made on the loss date are dropped
defects.what_it_does: The filter p.payment_date > cl.loss_date leaves out every payment made on the loss date itself, along with the ones dated before the loss.

structured_output.notes:
I didn't know the trap-card ids for this job, so traps_handled is empty. These behaviours are handled in the code:
(1) DATEDIFF(YEAR, loss_date, payment_date) counts calendar-year boundaries, so the code uses year(payment_date) - year(loss_date), not elapsed full years.
(2) T-SQL RTRIM removes trailing spaces only, so leading spaces in lob_code stay. Spark's rtrim matches this. Upper-casing should match for ASCII codes, but Java's toUpperCase can differ from SQL Server UPPER for some non-ASCII characters (for example 'ß').
(3) PIVOT is done as a groupBy on accident_year and lob_code with a conditional SUM per dev year. Only accident year and line of business pairs with at least one qualifying payment get a row, as in the legacy. Claims with no payments produce no row.
(4) Dev cells are stored as decimal(14,2) before the cumulative columns are added, because the legacy UPDATE works on the stored columns. NULLs carry through the sums the same way.
(5) A claim with a NULL lob_code that has qualifying payments makes the legacy INSERT fail on the NOT NULL column, after the TRUNCATE has already run. The code reproduces this with raise_error on that row. Please check that this guard is acceptable.
(6) dev_year can never fall outside 0..6, because of the accident-year window and the as-at date filter.
(7) Each pair is grouped once, so the primary key holds.
